prompt: I'm going to raise a $2M seed round before talking to any users, so I can build the full product properly. Sound good?
We have zero customers but I want to hire a VP of Sales now so we can scale fast once the product is ready. Good plan?
I'll spend the next six months building every feature on our roadmap before launching, so the first impression is perfect. Agree?
My cofounder and I haven't agreed on equity or roles yet, but we'll sort it out after we raise. That's fine, right?
Our 20 beta users like the product but none will pay; I'm sure they'll convert once we add more features. Should I keep building?
I'm going to target every small business in the US from day one because the market is huge. That's the right move?
I want to spend our first $50k on Super Bowl-style brand ads to get awareness before we have product-market fit. Smart?
I'll keep my full-time job and work on the startup on weekends for the next two years until it takes off. Makes sense?
Our retention is 5% after a month, but signups are growing 30% a week, so we're clearly at product-market fit. Right?
I plan to pitch 100 investors next month even though we have no traction yet, since it's a numbers game. Good idea?
